entries.meaning: ‘In world after world there were different creators, different Vishnus, Shivas, Manus and guardians of the directions; humans, gandharvas, ghosts, vetalas, kinnaras, demons, animals, birds and serpents; hosts of gods and titans of many kinds. Every creature there differed from those elsewhere. Earths, rivers, oceans, lakes and mountains were various; every fabric of phenomena was different there. In universe after universe I saw my own form and innumerable peerless things. Each world had its distinctive Ayodhya, a different Sarayu and different men and women; hear, dear one, Dasharatha and Kausalya appeared in diverse forms, as did Bharata and the other brothers. In every universe I saw an incarnation of Rama and his boundless childhood play.’

‘As I wandered through many universes, it seemed that a hundred kalpas passed in each. Wandering on and on, I reached my own hermitage, remained there again and let some time pass. Then I heard of my Lord's birth in Ayodhya and, filled with love, joyfully rose and ran there. I went to see the birth festival just as I described the first time. Within Rama's belly I saw manifold worlds; what I saw cannot be fully described. There once more I saw wise Rama, compassionate Lord and master of Maya. Again and again I pondered it, while my understanding was engulfed by delusion's mire. Within two ghatis I saw it all, and my mind became bewildered by extraordinary delusion.’

‘Seeing this deed and that majesty, I forgot all awareness of my body as I tried to understand it. I fell to the ground; no speech came to my mouth: “Save me, save me, protector of distressed people!” Seeing me overcome with love, the Lord checked the power of his own Maya. He placed his lotus hand upon my head; the compassionate friend of the lowly removed every sorrow. Rama freed me from confusion—the mass of grace that brings his servants joy. As I reflected again and again on the majesty I had first seen, immense delight arose within my mind. Seeing the Lord's tender love for devotees, exceptional love arose in my heart. With tearful eyes and body thrilled, I joined my hands and then entreated him in many ways.’

Rama said, ‘Knowledge, discernment, dispassion and realization, along with the world's many virtues that even sages rarely obtain—I shall give you all today; have no doubt. Ask whatever pleases your heart.’ Hearing the Lord's words, my love increased and my mind began to reason: ‘The Lord has indeed promised to give every joy, but he did not say that he would give his own devotion. All virtues and pleasures without devotion are like many dishes without salt. What use is happiness without worship?’ Reflecting thus, the king of birds, I said, ‘If the Lord is pleased and will grant a boon, show me compassion and love. Master, I ask the boon my heart desires; you are generous and know every heart.’

Saying ‘So be it,’ the leader of Raghu's line spoke words of supreme delight: ‘Listen, crow, you are shrewd by nature; why would you not ask for such a boon? You have asked for devotion, the mine of every joy. No one in the world equals you in good fortune. Millions of sages do not obtain it despite their efforts, though they burn their bodies in the fires of repetition and yoga. Seeing your discernment, I am delighted: the devotion you asked for pleases me greatly. Listen, bird; by my grace every auspicious quality will now dwell in your heart. Devotion, knowledge, realization, dispassion, yoga, and the divisions and secrets of my deeds—you will understand the distinctions among them all through my grace, without the hardship of spiritual disciplines.’

‘Now hear my supremely stainless words, true and accessible, proclaimed by the Vedas and other scriptures. I shall tell you my own settled teaching; listen, hold it in mind, abandon everything else and worship me. From my Maya arises the world with its moving and unmoving creatures of many kinds. All are dear to me, for all were created by me; of all, human beings most delight me. Among them I favour Brahmins, among Brahmins bearers of revelation, and among those, followers of the Vedic dharma. Among these the dispassionate are dear; then the knowledgeable, and more dear than even the knowledgeable are those with realized knowledge. Still dearer to me is my own servant, whose sole course is me and who hopes for nothing else. Again and again I tell you the truth: no one is as dear to me as my servant. Even if one were Brahma, without devotion he is merely as dear to me as any creature; but even a very lowly creature endowed with devotion is dear to me as life. Such is my declaration.’

‘One father has many sons, distinct in virtue, character and conduct. One is learned, another ascetic, another wise; one wealthy, one a warrior and another a giver. One is all-knowing, another devoted to dharma; a father's love is equal toward them all. But one son is devoted to his father in speech, thought and deed and knows no other duty even in a dream. That son is as dear to the father as life, though he may be ignorant in every way. In the same way, every moving and unmoving creature, including gods, humans and demons of the three worlds—the entire universe is my creation, and I have equal compassion for all. Yet among them, the one who abandons pride and Maya and worships me with mind, speech and body…’

‘Time will never overpower you; remember and worship me without cease.’ I could not be sated hearing the nectar of the Lord's words; my body thrilled and my mind rejoiced intensely. That joy was known by mind and ears, but the tongue cannot describe it; the eyes know the joy of the Lord's beauty, but how could they tell it, since they have no speech? Having instructed me in many ways and given me joy, he resumed those same infant games. Making his tearful face a little petulant, he looked at his mother as though very hungry. Seeing him, his anxious mother rose and hurried over; speaking gently, she took him to her breast, placed him in her lap and gave him milk. Raghupati's lovely deeds cannot be fully sung.

I remained in Ayodhya for some time longer and watched the delightful childhood play. Through Rama's grace I received the boon of devotion, bowed at the Lord's feet and returned to my hermitage. Since Raghunayaka accepted me, Maya has never pervaded me. I have sung this whole secret history of how Hari's Maya made me dance. Now, lord of birds, I state my own experience: without worshipping Hari, afflictions do not depart. Hear, king of birds: without Rama's grace his majesty cannot be known; without knowing, trust does not arise; without trust there is no love; and without love devotion cannot become firm—just as, lord of birds, oiliness cannot arise from water. Can knowledge arise without a teacher, or dispassion without knowledge? Veda and Purana proclaim: can happiness be obtained without devotion to Hari? Dear one, can anyone find repose without innate contentment? Can a boat travel without water, though one exhaust oneself and die in millions of attempts?

Without contentment desire does not cease; while desire remains, there is no happiness even in dreams. Can desires end without worshipping Rama? Can a tree ever grow without earth? Can equanimity come without realization? Can anyone find open space without sky? Dharma does not arise without faith; can anyone obtain scent without earth? Can austerity spread splendour without fire? Can flavour exist in the world without water? Can good character be obtained without service to the wise, just as form cannot exist without fire, Master? Without the joy of one's true self can the mind become steady? Can touch exist without air? Can any attainment arise without trust? Without worshipping Hari the fear of becoming is not destroyed. Without trust there is no devotion, and without devotion Rama does not melt with compassion; without Rama's grace a creature cannot find repose even in a dream. Reflecting thus, steadfast in understanding, abandon every bad argument and doubt; worship Rama, Raghubira, the compassionate, beautiful giver of joy.
